function: Interferon-responsive guanylate-binding GTPase involved in antimicrobial host defense.
evidence_context: Human whole-blood multicohort TB study identified GBP5 in a three-gene diagnostic panel; experimental human and mouse work also connects GBP5 to selected inflammasome responses.
hypothesis: A reporter of an interferon-associated host-response component shared by both classifier panels.
limitation: Whole-blood diagnostic association does not identify the plasma RNA source or establish TB specificity of GBP5 alone; RNA abundance does not measure inflammasome assembly.

function: Large scaffold protein that organizes signaling complexes; experimental evidence links AHNAK1 to T-cell calcium entry and NFAT signaling.
evidence_context: Ahnak1-deficient mouse CD4 T cells had impaired TCR-induced calcium entry, IL-2 production and proliferation; infection experiments used Leishmania major.
hypothesis: An immune-signaling or broader cellular-state component that may complement the myeloid/interferon genes.
limitation: The cited mechanism is principally mouse T-cell evidence, not human TB or plasma-source validation. Hallmark IL2–STAT5 membership is an expression-signature annotation, not proof of IL2–STAT5 activation.

function: Chromatin and transcription-associated regulator with context-dependent hematopoietic functions, including evidence related to megakaryocyte differentiation.
evidence_context: Human cell-line and cord-blood work linked JMJD1C to megakaryopoiesis and actin organization. Knockdown effects differed between K562 and MEG-01. An adult mouse knockout study found healthy hematopoiesis and JAK2 V617F-driven myeloproliferative disease initiation largely preserved.
hypothesis: A competing hematopoietic/platelet-associated or transcriptional-state component, rather than an assumed specific myeloid TB effector.
limitation: The 2022 study mainly used cell lines and did not assay platelet generation. Leukemia or megakaryocyte evidence does not establish a TB mechanism or prove normal adult hematopoiesis requires JMJD1C.

function: Myeloid-associated nuclear protein that helps regulate IRF7 expression and type I interferon amplification.
evidence_context: Human primary monocytes and THP-1 perturbation experiments showed MNDA supports IRF7 promoter recruitment of STAT2/RNA polymerase II and IFN-alpha induction after nucleic-acid or viral stimulation.
hypothesis: A bridge between myeloid RNA contribution and interferon-associated cellular state.
limitation: This functional study tested innate/antiviral signaling, not TB specificity. Myeloid association alone does not establish direct SPI1 regulation.

function: Lysozyme, an antimicrobial enzyme that hydrolyzes bacterial peptidoglycan; its RNA is a common myeloid marker.
evidence_context: Human TB PBMC single-cell research used LYZ with other markers to annotate myeloid cells; curated Reactome records its antimicrobial reaction and neutrophil-granule membership.
hypothesis: A marker of RNA sources and/or myeloid antimicrobial programs; test whether it follows monocyte/neutrophil contributions and broader panel-excluded programs.
limitation: The cited discovery single-cell cohort had four TB patients and four controls. Marker use is not evidence that LYZ alone is TB-specific, that all plasma LYZ is myeloid, or that lysozyme-mediated killing is increased.

function: Encodes PU.1, a transcription factor involved in hematopoietic differentiation and lineage-specific gene expression.
evidence_context: A human/murine experimental expression study found high PU.1 in mature human monocytes and peripheral-blood neutrophils; PU.1 also has lymphoid roles.
hypothesis: An immune-cell identity component that may covary with MNDA/LYZ and granulopoiesis-related expression.
limitation: SPI1 RNA is not a measurement of PU.1 protein abundance, DNA binding, target regulation or activity. Shared expression is insufficient to infer a SPI1→MNDA causal edge.

function: NIX protein participates in mitochondrial removal during reticulocyte maturation.
evidence_context: Knockout-model experiments connect NIX to erythroid mitochondrial clearance.
hypothesis: An erythroid or mitochondrial-quality-control component in the paper panel.
limitation: Plasma RNA does not measure mitophagy flux, and the mechanism is not evidence of TB specificity.

function: Transcription factor with experimentally supported roles in inflammatory macrophage responses.
evidence_context: Macrophage gain/loss-of-function experiments and myeloid perturbation; additional work in human monocyte-derived macrophages.
hypothesis: An inflammatory or cell-state contribution; the paper panel also has direct immune biology.
limitation: A conditional expression difference does not establish KLF6 activity or a specific macrophage polarization state.

function: Dysferlin is involved in membrane repair and has experimentally studied monocyte adhesion and phagocytosis roles.
evidence_context: Human monocytes/THP1 adhesion study; deficiency studies in patient and mouse systems.
hypothesis: A membrane/monocyte component that complements the paper panel’s shared GBP5 signal.
limitation: Results depend on experimental condition; higher RNA does not necessarily mean greater phagocytosis or identify the plasma source.

function: Actin/focal-adhesion scaffold associated with cell migration and survival.
evidence_context: Cell perturbation and localization experiments; broad cytoskeletal function.
hypothesis: A cellular-structure or source-state contribution, without a specific myeloid/TB assignment.
limitation: Migration effects are context dependent; no annotation in these two collections is not evidence of no biological function.

function: Poly(C)-binding RNA-associated protein with an experimentally demonstrated iron-chaperone function.
evidence_context: Biochemical, yeast and human-cell experiments support iron delivery to ferritin.
hypothesis: An RNA-processing/iron-handling component in the paper panel.
limitation: These functions do not establish iron redistribution, viral infection, or a TB-specific mechanism in these samples.
